name: Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung (FNF) Scholarship for Foreign Students from Non-EU Countries
requiredDocuments: Online application via the FNF application portal (all uploads as PDF, max 5 MB per document category; documents in German or English, translations done by the applicant)
Identification document (identity card or passport) — non-EU applicants must submit the pages with personal data and visa/residence status
University admission / certificate of enrollment (matriculation certificate must be available at the latest at admission to the scholarship programme; can be shown at the selection interview)
Diploma/degree qualifying for the relevant university studies (Bachelor/Master)
(Academic) transcripts (e.g. Table of Records, and Bachelor's/Diploma certificate if applicable)
If applicable, certificates of vocational training or professional activity

Two (2) letters of reference from university professors / scientific assistants (for a 1st-semester Master programme, references from the bachelor programme are accepted) — submitted directly by reviewers via a generated link, not by email/mail
Passport/ID page showing residence permit (to evidence the under-15-months-in-Germany condition)

timeline.notes: Two fixed application windows every year, recurring: 1-30 April and 1-31 October (deadlines 30 April and 31 October at 11:59 pm). Applications are only possible through the online portal during these windows. Interview-invitation notification by 8 February (April round) or 8 August (October round) at the latest. As of 2026-06 the April 2026 window has closed and the next window is 1-31 October 2026; these are standing annual dates taken verbatim from the official FAQ, not a one-off cycle. Non-European applicants still abroad may be invited to a video-call interview; everyone already in Germany must appear in person.

benefits: Monthly scholarship (living stipend) of up to 861 euros for student funding — non-repayable
Lump sum for study costs of 300 euros per month (paid to all fellows)
Monthly contributions to health insurance and long-term-care insurance
Non-material support: seminars, networking and the FNF fellow community (ideational support)
Funding initially granted for one year, extendable for a further year until completion of the master's (minimum funding period two semesters)
Stays abroad of up to 12 months related to the studies may be supported (travel, health insurance, study/research fees, living expenses) on a case-by-case basis
mustKnow: German required: B2-level German is essential. All application documents must be submitted in German, and the selection interview is conducted in German — even if your master's programme is taught entirely in English. (No formal language test is required to apply, but the interview is in German.)

Residence cap: you can only apply if you have NOT been in Germany for more than 15 months prior to the start of the scholarship (exceptions for prior research/study stays, which you must evidence with passport residence entries).

Living stipend, not tuition reimbursement: the award is a monthly stipend (up to 861 euros) + 300 euros/month study-cost lump sum + insurance. It does not separately pay tuition fees (German public universities are largely tuition-free). Gross income over 450 euros is offset against the scholarship.

Master's (or doctorate) full-time in Germany only — non-EU applicants cannot be funded for a bachelor's. LL.M, MBA, second degrees, part-time/distance courses, and projects/internships are not funded.
You must have at least two remaining semesters (the minimum funding period is two semesters); apply no later than the third-to-last semester before completing your studies.
Binational master's programmes must be taught more than 50% of the time in Germany to be eligible.
Two university-professor letters of reference are mandatory and must be submitted by the reviewers themselves via a generated link (not by email/mail).
Mandatory in-person/video selection interview before an independent committee; travel and accommodation for the selection conference are NOT reimbursed and there are no alternative interview dates.
No age limit and no application/processing fee stated. Double funding for the same purpose from another public institution is not allowed; FDP membership is not required.
Acceptance rate is not officially published by FNF — capacity-limited, so academically suitable applicants are sometimes rejected for lack of funding.

universities: Any German, EU-European or Swiss state or state-recognized university, university of applied sciences, art/educational/theological college (master's must be full-time in Germany for non-EU applicants)

duration: Initially 1 year, extendable for a further year until completion of the master's (minimum funding period 2 semesters)
eligibleNationalities: Foreign students from non-EU countries doing a full-time master's in Germany. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible (Bangladesh is a non-EU country). There is no closed bilateral country list; eligibility is by status, not a partner-country list.
languageRequirements: B2-level German is essential. Application documents must be in German and the selection interview is in German, even for English-taught programmes. No language test certificate is required at the application stage; no IELTS/TOEFL is requested either.
ageLimit: No age limit (official FAQ: 'Is there an age limit for the application? No.')
fundingCovers: Possible study-abroad support up to 12 months
monthlyStipend: Up to 861 euros/month student stipend + 300 euros/month study-cost lump sum (EUR)
bondObligation: None (the scholarship does not have to be repaid; no return-home bond stated)
renewalConditions: Funding initially for one year; an extension for a further year may be applied for until completion of studies, subject to continued eligibility and academic progress.
